title: Worksheet 10: Loop Conditions and Boolean Logic
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: The condition used to control a while loop is always a boolean expression, meaning it must evaluate to either true or false each time it is checked, determining whether the loop should continue running or stop. Loop conditions often involve comparing values, such as checking whether a variable is less than, greater than, or equal to a specific number, and these comparisons can also be combined using logical operators like "and" and "or" to create more complex conditions. For example, a loop might be written to continue running only while a variable called "attempts" is less than 3 AND a boolean variable called "success" is still false, meaning the loop would only continue if both of those individual conditions are true at the same time; if either one becomes false, such as "attempts" reaching 3, or "success" becoming true, the entire combined condition would become false, and the loop would stop. Understanding exactly how a loop's condition will evaluate, especially when multiple comparisons are combined together, is critical for predicting exactly how many times a loop will actually repeat.
